name: Etidronic acid
description: Etidronic acid (CAS 2809-21-4 ), commonly known as HEDP or Oxyethylidenediphosphonic acid, is a phosphonate chelating agent used across water treatment, industrial cleaning, and personal care manufacturing. It binds metal ions and inhibits scale formation, preventing corrosion and deposit buildup in process systems and formulated products. In water treatment and oilfield operations, HEDP controls calcium carbonate and calcium sulfate scale. This chemical is essential for cooling towers, boilers, and injection systems, effectively extending equipment service life. Personal care formulators use it as a stabilizer in oxidative hair color and bleaching products. It sequesters trace metals that would otherwise degrade peroxide systems, ensuring product stability. Textile and paper processors apply it to prevent metal-catalyzed degradation during bleaching and dyeing processes. This application protects fiber quality and ensures process consistency across manufacturing lines. In industrial cleaning and detergent formulations, it disperses iron and hardness ions to improve wash performance. The agent prevents redeposition of minerals on surfaces during the cleaning cycle. Etidronic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at sixty percent active content for industrial use. While other concentrations are available for specific applications, Technical grade is the standard for water treatment. Higher-purity grades serve personal care and specialty formulation markets globally. Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers or drums is the typical commercial format for this product.
